decisions.reason: The source changes the second V by excluding the Hero V's expressive right-arm gesture and relating it instead to the left-arm design philosophy, but a complete same-message MODIFY already records that change and removes the obsolete terminal-inheritance attributes.

A complete same-message MODIFY already records the narrower proportions, restrained expression, left-arm architectural DNA, and exclusion of the expressive right-arm gesture from the remaining alphabet.
A same-message MODIFY already records the newly distinguished system roles of the Hero V's expressive right arm and restrained left arm.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Kenji,

Seeing the four directions as complete systems made the evaluation both enjoyable and much more productive—thank you.

Of the set, the third concept draws me most strongly. I don’t consider it the final solution, but it is the first direction that seems genuinely focused on building a cohesive architectural language rather than merely changing finishing details. Its V proportions also come closest to what I have envisioned.

Reviewing the concepts led me to an important realization: the Hero V actually contains two distinct design languages. The crucial distinction for this next round is between its right and left arms. The expressive right arm is the identity’s signature and must remain exclusive to the Hero V and the É accent; that gesture should not recur across the rest of the alphabet.

The left arm serves a different purpose. Its restraint, confidence, and structural clarity should supply the architectural DNA for the remaining letters. That does not mean repeating its geometry, but rather applying the same design philosophy.

For the next exploration, please continue from the third concept with this revised thinking. The present letterforms are too wide and somewhat too expressive. They should become narrower, more refined, disciplined, and cohesive while remaining unmistakably custom and not reminiscent of any existing typeface.

I’m looking forward to seeing how this direction develops.

value_updates.shared_terminal_rule: The Hero V and É accent share the expressive right-arm signature gesture; the second V and remaining alphabet must not repeat it.

decisions.reason: The source distinguishes geometric design languages and signature-gesture usage, but it does not change the deferred champagne-metal treatment or the material-language relationship.
The source refines individual letterform construction and proportions without changing the current composition, kerning, case-treatment, hierarchy, or fixed-reference rules.
The revised allocation of expressive and restrained geometry is compatible with the existing brand-expression goals and does not necessarily alter any of their current attributes.
The source does not change the decision to use a proprietary wordmark without a separate icon or monogram.
The letterform design-language revision does not change the requirement to deliver final production-ready artwork.
